entry.summary: Since 2016 travel from mainland Australia to Norfolk Island is domestic. Australian citizens need photo ID (such as a driver's licence), not a passport, though operators still recommend one.
entry.other: New Zealand and other foreign citizens need a passport and must meet mainland Australian entry rules, including any visa. Flights still use international terminals.
entry.next_check: Read the Australian Government's Norfolk Island travel information page (timed out on 31 October 2026).

health-entry.notes: Yellow fever rule as reported to WHO in 2021. WHO lists Norfolk Island under Australia. WHO advises confirming with the embassy before travel.
conditional: Yellow fever certificate: Proof of vaccination against yellow fever is required for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and with the exception of Galápagos Islands in Ecuador, and for travellers having transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of a country with risk of yellow fever transmission and with the same exception as mentioned above

seasons-and-flow.climate: Wettest: March, June and July. Driest: February, September and October. Hottest: February (22.5°C average). Coolest: August (16.0°C average). Country-wide averages for 1991 to 2020; coasts, mountains and the far north or south can differ a lot.

events.what: The appointment of the Norfolk Island Regional Council administrators runs to this date
events.effect: Local governance may change; an election for a five-member Transition Assembly has been announced but not yet dated

year-ahead.note: The Australian Government plans a five-member Norfolk Island Transition Assembly (no law-making power) as the first stage of a new local governance model. No election date had been published when checked.

own_names: Norfolk Island; Norf'k is the island's own language, a mix of old English and Tahitian.
greetings_and_words: Yorlyi kam luk orn: come and have a look.
culture-and-protocol.welcome_and_acknowledgement: Anniversary Bounty Day, 8 June, marks the arrival of the Pitcairn families in 1856; descendants are a large part of today's community.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: The Norfolk Island community; no formal visitor protocol was found in the tourism body's published pages. Ask locally on community events and Bounty Day participation.

laws.rule: Norfolk Island is an Australian external territory where Commonwealth laws apply and New South Wales laws apply as modified by the Norfolk Island Applied Laws Ordinance 2016; read the NSW Act with the Ordinance's schedule for the Norfolk Island version.
